column1: # coupid6 run 1, 2026-09-02. Manual dwell observations captured over the UART
# link after the board's HTTP server wedged (errno 23, descriptor exhaustion)
# and the 5 s poll capture stopped at 22:27:28 / 197 lines.
# Ambient at run start: 25.66 / 25.54 / 25.34 C (zones 0/1/2).
# dwell_target_c  t_into_dwell_s  actual0 actual1 actual2  duty0 duty1 duty2
# CAVEAT: rows above are single INSTANTANEOUS duty samples read over UART, not
# averages over a settled window. Duty fluctuates, dwells are 600 s against a
# ~265 s tau (only ~2.3 tau, so each zone is still creeping), and ambient is
# assumed shared at 25.5 C. Use the 5 s poll captures
# (coupid6_run1.jsonl + coupid6_run1_part2.jsonl) and average over the settled
# tail of each dwell before drawing any conclusion about linearity.
# NOT SETTLED. z0 duty rose 0.13 (382 s) -> 0.15 (430 s) -> 0.17 (552 s) while
# its temperature DRIFTED DOWN 46.2 -> 45.8 -> 45.3 C. The 600 s dwell is only
# ~2.3 tau against the ~265 s zone time constant, so none of these dwells reach
# steady state and the apparent "z0 duty is flat with temperature" reading was
# an artifact of that, not evidence about linearity.
# CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXPERIMENT: coupid6's 10 min dwells are too short to
# measure DC gain. The single-zone excitation profiles (#4/#5/#6) use 35 min
# dwells, which is ~8 tau and adequate. Treat coupid6 as ramp/trend data and
# take the DC-gain measurement from the single-zone runs.
# ZONE 2 HEADROOM: at the 70 C dwell zone 2 sits at 0.81-0.83 duty and only just
# holds target, while zone 0 overshoots +2.2 C at 0.09-0.11. Against the 80 C
# zone ceiling this is close to saturation, so zone 2 likely cannot hold much
# above 70 C on this rig. Worth confirming deliberately before any profile is
# written that assumes it can.
# ZONE 2 AUTHORITY AT 70 C -- CORRECTED. An earlier note here said z2 "cannot
# hold 70 C"; that was premature and is wrong. Trajectory through the dwell:
#   405 s  69.6 C  duty 0.92  (below target, duty rising)
#   446 s  70.0 C  duty 0.89  (AT target, duty easing -- equilibrium reached)
# So z2 DOES hold 70 C, at ~0.89 duty, with roughly 10 % margin left. What is
# real is the ASYMMETRY: z0 holds the same setpoint at 0.14-0.15 while z2 needs
# ~0.89, a 6x difference in required duty for identical temperature. The
# headroom is genuinely thin near 70 C and z2 would be the zone that saturates
# first, but the ceiling has NOT been reached here. Determine the real ceiling
# deliberately (a dedicated climb until z2 pins at 1.0 and falls behind) rather
# than inferring it from this run.
